FINAL EXECUTION BLOCK — COMPLETE IVX CODE AND AUTONOMOUS DEPLOYMENT

OWNER DIRECTIVE

Complete the IVX codebase and autonomous deployment pipeline now.

Do not return another explanation of the same blockers.

Do not stop after identifying an error.

Proceed through the full chain:

DIAGNOSE
→ FIX
→ TEST
→ COMMIT
→ PUSH
→ CI GREEN
→ OWNER AUTHORIZE
→ WORKER EXECUTE
→ DEPLOY
→ VERIFY
→ PROOF

==================================================
CURRENT VERIFIED BLOCKERS
==================================================

1. GitHub Actions is failing at:

Android Release Consistency
→ Validate configured APK release references

2. The final autonomous deployment requires a real owner-authorized action from inside IVX.

Everything else must continue now.

==================================================
PHASE 1 — FIX THE ANDROID CI FAILURE
==================================================

Open the latest failing GitHub Actions run for:

.github/workflows/ivx-ci.yml

Return:

- Workflow run ID
- Commit SHA
- Failed job
- Failed step
- Exact command
- First meaningful error
- Final error
- Exit code
- File and line
- Root cause

Do not answer only:

“Validate configured APK release references failed.”

Find the exact mismatch.

Audit:

- APK filename
- APK expected path
- Android applicationId
- versionName
- versionCode
- release build profile
- artifact path
- checksum reference
- signing configuration
- build output folder
- obsolete APK references
- old package names
- old build numbers
- old debug APK references
- documentation used by CI

Search specifically for stale references to:

- ivx-holdings-v1.4.0.apk
- ivx-holdings-v1.4.3-build11-final.apk
- debug APK names
- obsolete artifact directories
- obsolete application IDs
- obsolete version codes

For every mismatch return:

- File
- Line
- Current value
- Correct value
- Fix applied

==================================================
PHASE 2 — FIX WITHOUT WEAKENING CI
==================================================

Correct the root cause.

Do not:

- disable the failing step
- use continue-on-error
- skip Android validation
- hardcode a fake APK
- claim an artifact exists when it does not
- remove release consistency protection

The validation must reflect the real current Android release configuration.

Run locally:

- Android release consistency check
- TypeScript check
- Unit tests
- Integration tests
- Security scan
- Secret scan
- Dependency scan
- Independence audit
- Backend build
- Worker build
- Website build
- Expo validation

Required result:

All mandatory checks exit 0.

==================================================
PHASE 3 — STANDARDIZE ANDROID RELEASE
==================================================

Create one canonical Android release configuration.

Return:

- Application ID
- Version name
- Version code
- Release profile
- Output APK filename
- Output artifact path
- Signing mode
- API base URL
- Build command
- Expected checksum file

Requirements:

- No debug signing represented as production signing
- No obsolete APK name
- No conflicting application IDs
- No conflicting version values
- No Play Store submission required now
- Direct-install release APK supported

==================================================
PHASE 4 — COMMIT AND PUSH
==================================================

Commit all required fixes to:

Repository:
ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform

Branch:
main

Return:

- Files changed
- Commit message
- Commit SHA
- Push status
- GitHub main HEAD SHA

Do not stop after local testing.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — RUN CI UNTIL GREEN
==================================================

Run or trigger the real GitHub Actions workflow.

Required jobs:

- Backend tests
- Android release consistency
- Type checks
- Security checks
- Secret scan
- Dependency scan
- Independence audit
- Build validation
- APK build if configured for this trigger

Return:

- Workflow run ID
- Commit SHA
- Each job status
- Start time
- End time
- Final result

CI must be green before production promotion.

If another job fails:

- diagnose it
- fix it
- commit it
- push it
- rerun CI

Repeat until all required jobs pass.

==================================================
PHASE 6 — VERIFY THE FULL CODEBASE
==================================================

Audit all major code areas:

- Website
- Expo app
- Android app
- iOS project
- Backend API
- Public chat
- Owner chat
- Owner authentication
- Members
- Investors
- Buyers
- Properties
- Deals
- Reels
- Media
- Documents
- Transactions
- Treasury
- Commissions
- Audit jobs
- Autonomous worker
- Proof ledger
- Monitoring
- Rollback

For every area return:

- PASS
- PARTIAL
- FAIL
- Exact blocker
- Exact file
- Exact next action

Do not claim 100% if any critical module is still failing.

==================================================
PHASE 7 — FINISH OWNER AUTHORIZATION INSIDE IVX
==================================================

Do not ask the owner to paste a Supabase access token into Rork chat.

Complete the owner-only IVX action:

AUTHORIZE AUTONOMOUS DEPLOYMENT

Place it inside:

- Owner Settings
or
- Admin Hub
or
- IVX IA Owner Dashboard

The button must use the current live Supabase session:

supabase.auth.getSession()

If session is expired:

- call supabase.auth.refreshSession()
- retry once
- if refresh fails, require normal owner login

Do not create an infinite retry loop.

The owner action must authorize:

- exact action
- exact repository
- exact branch
- exact commit SHA
- exact worker ID
- exact environment
- short expiration
- single use

==================================================
PHASE 8 — GENERATE WORKER AUTHORIZATION
==================================================

Use the deployed endpoint:

POST /api/ivx/senior-developer/generate-worker-access

Requirements:

- Validate live Supabase owner JWT
- Confirm caller is the registered IVX owner
- Generate short-lived worker authorization
- Store only SHA-256 hash
- Never store raw token
- Never log raw token
- Bind to exact commit SHA
- Bind to exact action
- Bind to exact worker ID
- Expire in 5–15 minutes
- Single-use only
- Write issuance to proof ledger

Expected results:

- Valid owner: HTTP 201
- Missing session: HTTP 401
- Invalid/expired session: HTTP 401
- Non-owner: HTTP 403

==================================================
PHASE 9 — EXECUTE ONE REAL AUTONOMOUS DEPLOYMENT JOB
==================================================

Create one real owner-approved deployment job.

Required job lifecycle:

- owner_authenticated
- approval_created
- authorization_issued
- job_queued
- worker_authenticated
- token_consumed
- checkout_started
- tests_started
- tests_passed
- build_started
- build_passed
- deployment_started
- deployment_live
- health_verified
- version_verified
- proof_written
- job_completed

Required worker:

ivx-senior-dev-01

Required repository:

ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform

Required branch:

main

Required SHA:

exact approved GitHub HEAD

==================================================
PHASE 10 — DEPLOY THE EXACT APPROVED SHA
==================================================

Deploy to the existing services only.

API:
ivx-holdings-platform

Worker:
ivx-senior-dev-01

Website:
existing IVX production website service

Do not:

- create a new repository
- create a new Render service
- deploy an old commit
- substitute another SHA
- bypass CI
- bypass owner approval

Return:

- GitHub HEAD SHA
- Approved SHA
- API deployment ID
- Worker deployment ID
- Website deployment ID
- API live SHA
- Worker live SHA
- Website live version
- Deployment timestamps

All applicable SHAs must match.

==================================================
PHASE 11 — VERIFY LIVE PRODUCTION
==================================================

Verify:

WEBSITE
- https://ivxholding.com
- /robots.txt
- /sitemap.xml

API
- /health
- /version

CHAT
- normal public chat
- protected deploy request

OWNER
- owner endpoint without auth
- owner endpoint with valid owner session

WORKER
- status
- heartbeat
- queue depth
- latest job

Expected:

- Website HTTP 200
- robots.txt HTTP 200
- sitemap.xml HTTP 200
- /health HTTP 200
- /version HTTP 200
- /version SHA matches GitHub HEAD
- Public chat HTTP 200
- Protected action safely blocked when unauthorized
- Missing owner auth returns 401
- Valid owner action succeeds
- Worker heartbeat healthy
- Job status completed

==================================================
PHASE 12 — PROVE REPLAY PROTECTION
==================================================

After successful token consumption:

- attempt to reuse the same authorization
- reject the second use
- do not create a second job
- do not create a second deployment

Return:

- Replay timestamp
- HTTP status
- Error code
- Duplicate job count
- Duplicate deployment count

Expected:

Replay rejected: YES
Duplicate job: NO
Duplicate deployment: NO

==================================================
PHASE 13 — WRITE AND VERIFY PROOF LEDGER
==================================================

The proof ledger must record:

- Owner authorization ID
- Owner identifier
- Job ID
- Worker ID
- Repository
- Branch
- Approved SHA
- Executed SHA
- CI run ID
- Test result
- Build result
- Deployment IDs
- Live SHAs
- Health result
- Version result
- Replay rejection
- Completion timestamp
- Final status

Restart the worker safely and verify:

- completed job remains completed
- ledger remains available
- token remains consumed
- no duplicate execution occurs
- heartbeat returns

==================================================
PHASE 14 — COMPLETE RORK INDEPENDENCE CLEANUP
==================================================

Only after CI is green and production is verified:

- remove obsolete EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_* variables
- remove obsolete toolkit variables
- remove inactive Rork CDN references
- remove inactive Rork SDK references
- remove rork.json only after replacement CI no longer requires it
- preserve useful IVX-owned audit scripts
- verify no Rork runtime traffic exists

Required final counts:

- Active Rork API calls: 0
- Active Rork SDKs: 0
- Active Rork packages: 0
- Active Rork domains: 0
- Active Rork environment variables: 0
- Active Rork build dependencies: 0
- Active Rork deployment dependencies: 0
- Active Rork authentication dependencies: 0
- Active Rork telemetry: 0

==================================================
FINAL EVIDENCE
==================================================

CODE
- Repository:
- Owner:
- Branch:
- GitHub HEAD SHA:
- Files changed:
- Final commit SHA:

CI
- Workflow run ID:
- Android consistency:
- Backend tests:
- Type checks:
- Security:
- Final status:

OWNER AUTHORIZATION
- Owner session valid:
- Authorization ID:
- Approved action:
- Approved SHA:
- Worker ID:
- Issued:
- Expires:
- Hash-only storage:
- Consumed:

AUTONOMOUS JOB
- Job ID:
- Worker ID:
- Initial status:
- Final status:
- Started:
- Completed:
- Proof ledger ID:

RENDER API
- Service ID:
- Deployment ID:
- Live SHA:
- Status:
- Boot time:

RENDER WORKER
- Service ID:
- Deployment ID:
- Live SHA:
- Status:
- Heartbeat:
- Last completed job:

WEBSITE
- Deployment ID:
- URL:
- HTTP status:
- Live version:

LIVE VERIFICATION
- /health:
- /version:
- Public chat:
- Unauthorized owner request:
- Valid owner request:
- Worker status:

SECURITY
- Replay rejected:
- Duplicate job:
- Duplicate deployment:
- Secret scan:
- Rork dependency guard:

ROLLBACK
- Current stable SHA:
- Previous stable SHA:
- Rollback available:
- Recovery verified:

==================================================
FINAL PASS CONDITIONS
==================================================

Mark COMPLETE only when:

- Android CI failure is fixed
- GitHub Actions is green
- Code is committed and pushed
- GitHub HEAD is verified
- Owner authorizes from inside IVX
- Worker receives single-use authorization
- Worker checks out the IVX repository
- Tests pass
- Builds pass
- Exact approved SHA is deployed
- API and worker live SHAs match approved SHA
- /health returns HTTP 200
- /version returns the approved SHA
- Public chat works
- Proof ledger is written
- Replay is rejected
- No duplicate deployment occurs
- Worker restart does not repeat the job
- Rollback path exists
- Rork is not required in the production deployment chain

FINAL STATUS

IVX CODE COMPLETION:
PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL

ANDROID CI:
PASS / FAIL

AUTONOMOUS DEPLOYMENT:
PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL

IVX INDEPENDENCE:
PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL

Do not return another architecture report.

Fix the Android CI failure first, then continue through the complete deployment chain and return only verified evidence.
